tasks.short: Study drawings to determine workpiece layouts and templates

steps.what: Study blueprints or layouts to determine workpiece layout and template requirements

tasks.design: Retain drawing interpretation and workpiece assessment with the worker using {DOCS}. A digital drawing does not establish that layout choices or physical template work can be removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layout choices depend on the drawing and actual workpiece condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing drawings provide dimensions and reference geometry.
tasks.still_hard: Translate the drawing into a workable approach for the material.
tasks.human_edge: Notice drawing ambiguities and physical constraints.
tasks.altitude: Own understanding of the layout before finishing work.

evidence.claim: Drawing interpretation for hand finishing retains full time; no structured repeatable layout computation is established.

assumptions: The baseline is studying and interpreting drawings, not an invented data-entry task.
No new automation service or added upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Drawing formats and repeated template needs
research_questions: Are repeated geometric calculations measurable separately from interpreting the workpiece?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Drawing interpretation and layout judgement remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select files and abrasives for hand finishing

steps.what: Select files or abrasives for materials, workpiece shapes, stock removal and specified finishes

tasks.design: Keep abrasive and file selection with the worker, referring to specifications in {DOCS}. Reference charts support the choice but do not remove assessment of the actual surface and stock to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tool suitability depends on material, geometry and required finish.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing specifications and tool references support selection.
tasks.still_hard: Choose a tool that removes stock without damaging the workpiece.
tasks.human_edge: Assess the physical surface and likely finishing behaviour.

evidence.claim: Abrasive selection retains physical and material judgement; no complete structured selection rule is assumed.

assumptions: The baseline is selection against actual workpiece condition rather than a repeated catalogue-entry process.
No automatic material classification or stock-removal estimate is assumed.
No new automation or maintenance is added.
research_questions: Would existing reference charts address repeated selection questions without adding data capture?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Physical tool-selection judgement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record product and processing data on required forms

steps.what: Capture product identifiers and observed processing data in the job record
Record captured product and processing data on the specified form layout
Check product and processing entries for omissions and reconcile the completed form

tasks.design: Configure a native job form in {OPS_SYSTEM} to reuse the worker's captured entries in the required {DOCS} layout. Observation, measurement, capture and reconciliation remain human; the form produces no inferred quality or completion verdict.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observed processing details may be copied from job notes onto a specified form.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational records can populate fixed form fields.
tasks.still_hard: Ensure recorded details reflect the actual work and explain missing observations.
tasks.human_edge: Verify the truth and completeness of production records.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated form entry while protecting factual capture.

reach.task: Agree required processing fields and correction rules

evidence.claim: Native forms can reuse captured production entries in fixed layouts; the task-specific design and savings are model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the worker produces job ID, product or batch ID, operation, date, quantity, process observations and any required measured values with units; its 45 hours includes observation, measurement and capture.
The supervisor defines required field names and allowed process labels; two added other-role hours cover changes and record clarification.
Missing or inconsistent entries return to manual correction in s3; there is no free sensor feed, discrepancy code or quality flag.
Use native OPS_SYSTEM form configuration before custom integration; six additional focal hours cover field mappings and reconciliation checks.
Already automatic or single-entry forms earn no new saving; physical finishing time is outside this recording baseline.
research_questions: Does native form population save copying time after observation, capture and reconciliation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70; gross 30 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 24. E1 range 0-15 allows single-entry forms and variable processing fields; capture remains counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated production form entry while retaining physical assessment and finishing judgement.
role.ambitious_version: A hand finishing worker who records processing facts once where possible and retains responsibility for physical workpiece and tool judgement.
